questiontext.text:
A written proof that \(n^2 - 1\) is divisible by 8 for every odd number \(n\) begins: ‘Let \(n\) be an odd number.’

Which of these could correctly be the next line? Select all that apply.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Since \(n\) is odd, the definition of odd gives an integer \(k\) with \(n = 2k + 1\). ‘For some integer \(k\)’ says that such a \(k\) exists, and the proof then works with it. The \(k\) depends on \(n\) (for \(n = 11\), \(k = 5\)), so it is not a fixed number, and it is not ‘every integer’. Writing \(n = 2k - 1\) for some integer \(k\) works equally well: it describes the same numbers, and leads to \(n^2 - 1 = 4k(k - 1)\), the same proof. So the third and fifth lines are correct.

  • ‘For every integer \(k\)’ would mean that \(n\) equals \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\) all at once.

  • ‘Where \(k = 1\)’ makes \(n = 3\), so the rest of the proof would be about one number only.

  • \(n^2 - 1 = 8k\) is the conclusion. It may not be written down until it has been proved.

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the first line of Solution 4.2, the solution of Example 4.1 (p. 12), in Section 4 of Bokhove, C., Thoma, A., Gammack, D., Yu, L. H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Each says that \(n\) equals \(2k + 1\) (or \(2k - 1\)) for one particular integer \(k\), which exists because \(n\) is odd.
‘For every integer \(k\)’ would mean that \(n\) equals \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\) all at once. But \(n\) is one odd number: how many values of \(k\) can go with it?

node.description: Diagnostic: a particular value of k

truefeedback.text: With \(k = 1\), \(n\) would be 3, so the rest of the proof would be about \(n = 3\) only. To prove the statement for every odd \(n\), \(k\) must stand for whichever integer goes with \(n\).
\(n^2 - 1 = 8k\) is what the proof is trying to show. Writing it as the next line assumes the conclusion, so the proof would be circular.

falsefeedback.text: What you have selected is correct, but one more line could also come next. Look for another line that says no more than ‘\(n\) is odd’ already tells you.

qtest.description: Only one of the two correct lines
